dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Broncos Honor Tom Jackson With 38-24 Victory Over Raiders
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Denver (8-2) secured the AFC's #2 seed following a three-touchdown performance by Jonah Coleman and a Ja'Quan McMillian pick-six. The victory served as a tribute to Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, who passed away Friday.
bullets: Running back Jonah Coleman recorded a historic 111-yard, three-touchdown rushing performance, including a 7-yard score to finalize the 38-24 win [S4](https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/the-way-he-played-today-was-special-rb-jonah-coleman-posts-historic-111-yard-3-touchdown-rushing-performance-vs-raiders) [S13](https://www.denverbroncos.com/video/rb-jonah-coleman-finds-the-end-zone-for-7-yard-touchdown-broncos-vs-raiders).

Cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza for a 35-yard touchdown return, helping Denver maintain a +5 turnover differential [S12](https://www.denverbroncos.com/video/cb-ja-quan-mcmillian-records-35-yard-pick-six-broncos-vs-raiders).

Head Coach Sean Payton awarded the game ball to the family of Tom Jackson, honoring the "Orange Crush" legend 48 hours after his death at age 75 [S6](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50569388/broncos-coach-sean-payton-game-ball-tom-jackson-family).

Despite the win, Denver must address a #31 ranked 3rd-down conversion rate (32.4%) before facing the Pittsburgh Steelers' top-ranked rushing efficiency in Week 12 [S2](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50563342/week-11-sunday-games-takeaways-questions-2026).
